title: Verifiable chain-of-custody for admin audit events with regional retention enforcement
creator: Lara Chen
description: Add a provable chain-of-custody for admin activity events (console/admin API/config changes) that enforces per-region retention settings and writes tamper-resistant evidence to WORM-backed storage. Deliverables: event signing using customer- or account-scoped KMS keys, append-only ledger format with periodic notarized checkpoints, retention enforcement engine that prevents premature deletion based on residency policy, and automated evidence export for audits.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions (role changes, RBAC grants, configuration patches, API key rotations) are emitted to the new append-only ledger format with an HMAC or asymmetric signature per event.
Ledger checkpoints (Merkle root or signed digest) are published every 10 minutes and stored in a WORM container with retention metadata per-region.
Retention policy evaluation enforces regional residency rules: delete/expiration requests for data in a region must be blocked if policy requires local hold.
Automated export tool can produce a verifiable audit bundle for legal/compliance requests that includes signed checkpoints and a manifest.
Migration job to convert last 24 months of existing admin logs to the ledger format completes successfully in staging and preserves event ordering and signatures.
Security review sign-off (threat model + KMS integration) is recorded in Confluence and the PR includes verification tests.
implementation_notes: Use account-scoped asymmetric keys stored in KMS for signing events; fall back to service key for legacy tenants with opt-in migration.
Ledger entry = base64(json_event) + signature + sequence_id + region_tag. Sequence IDs assigned by regional ingestion proxy to preserve ordering without central bottleneck.
Checkpointing: build a Merkle tree of the last N events per region; publish Merkle root as signed checkpoint to WORM and to a globally replicated metadata service for quick verification.

Retention enforcement: attach canonical retention metadata to each ledger entry and implement policy engine that returns enforcement decision; deletion APIs verify policy and check presence of WORM escrow flag.
WORM storage options: hosted S3 Object Lock (governance mode) for Hosted accounts, on-prem WORM appliance for Private, and an encrypted escrow bucket for Dedicated.
Provide an export API that returns a signed bundle: events, checkpoint manifest, KMS public keys, and verification instructions for auditors.
Design trade-offs: central sequence allocator would simplify ordering but adds latency; opted for regional sequencers to keep write tail latency low at cost of slightly more complex verification.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Start with a dry-run migration in staging for last 90 days; verify sequence and checkpoint accuracy.
Phase 2: Canary migrate 5% of tenants in a non-production region; validate exports with compliance team.
Phase 3: Full run for tenants with compliance opt-in, followed by background conversion for remaining historical data while keeping live writes dual-wired to old+new sinks.
Rollback: if signature verification fails or ordering anomalies > 0.1%, pause and revert to dual-write mode while retaining raw logs for reprocessing.
test_plan: Unit tests for signature generation/verification using mocked KMS keys.
Integration tests for regional sequencer ordering under load (1000 rps sustained).
Chaos test: simulate delayed checkpoint writes and ensure export bundles are still verifiable.
E2E compliance test: auditor script verifies a produced bundle against public keys and replayed sequence.
